Physics · Ohm's law and resistance What Section 3 stimuli hand you

A wire with its diameter halved, and a question about the new current. The trap: scaling by 2, not the 4 that area (diameter squared) gives.

This week's Stemlord · episode 1

The Stemlord writes the questions.
You see straight through them.

Every Wednesday he dresses ordinary science up as something terrifying.
Have a go, then move the science underneath.

A deep-sea squid pumps blood through vessels of varying width… at 3,000 metres. Diabolical!

Blood flow through a vessel = pressure difference ÷ resistance. One vessel narrows and its resistance doubles, at the same pressure difference. What happens to the flow?

It’s 2. Flow = pressure ÷ resistance, so double the resistance and the flow halves. It’s Ohm’s law, with blood instead of current. The squid is new.
